purpose: Every child deserves a wonderful life.
mission: Pinnacle’s purpose is to help children grow toward self-sufficiency and participation in mainstream life, with the support and accommodations each child needs.
positioning: A connected developmental journey: understand present abilities, identify useful next goals, coordinate support, practise in everyday life, track and correct the plan, and reassess progress toward participation.

stages.title: Understand the child’s abilities
stages.text: Begin with what the child can do, their interests and the everyday situations where support would help. Pinnacle describes 17 developmental domains, 79 abilities and 349 skills, supported by 591 observations and an AbilityScore on a 0–1000 scale. These are different layers of its developmental framework.
stages.family: A starting point the family and care team can discuss together.
stages.source: Company walkthrough, page 26; September handout, pages 5–6

stages.title: Build a child-specific direction
stages.text: Connect the observed abilities with priorities, readiness goals and a plan for this child. The dossier describes a personal development kernel: a persistent child-specific record of measurements, responses to techniques, environment and history that informs subsequent recommendations.
stages.family: Clarity about what to work on next, why it matters and who will help.
stages.source: Evidence Dossier, pages 48–49; BIS schedule, page 2

stages.title: Coordinate professional support
stages.text: Use the plan to coordinate appropriate therapies and intervention. Pinnacle describes practitioners, parents, caregivers and educators contributing to the programme; software supports professional judgement and shared goals.
stages.family: People working from an agreed direction across the child’s support team.
stages.source: September handout, pages 5–7; MD-5 intended use

stages.title: Make the plan part of everyday life
stages.text: The September handout describes 7–9 techniques selected for the child’s programme each day. Parents and other caregivers receive guidance for practice connected to the child’s current abilities and goals; the care team agrees what is appropriate.
stages.family: A practical way to carry support into home routines and other everyday settings.

stages.title: Observe, track and correct
stages.product: Fusion Module · people in the loop
stages.text: Record how practice goes and bring observations from the family and professionals back into review. The BIS schedule names parent, family, caregiver, therapist and clinical tracking and correction through the Fusion Module.
stages.family: A plan that can respond when an activity, setting or support needs to change.

stages.title: Reassess and explain the trajectory
stages.text: Compare the child’s present abilities with their own earlier assessments and review the next priorities. The company walkthrough describes a monthly AbilityScore refresh; the Whitebook also describes monthly review. The care team should explain the schedule and any child-specific changes.
stages.family: An understandable record of change over time, connected to daily-life goals—not a judgement of the child’s worth.

stages.title: Grow toward self-sufficiency and participation
stages.text: Work toward communication, daily living, learning, relationships and participation in school and community. The BIS scope names seven readiness indexes, including Self Sufficiency and Mainstream Inclusion. Continue reassessment and support as needs change.
stages.family: A wonderful life defined with the child and family, including the supports that make participation possible.

boundary: This is Pinnacle’s documented developmental-support approach. PinnacleAI® GPT-OS v1.0.0 is a non-diagnostic Class B SaMD for ages 0–12 under the supplied MD-5. A programme, score or licence does not guarantee independence, school entry or a particular outcome. Inclusion is a right; it is not conditional on a score.
measurementNote: The company walkthrough labels 17 domains, 79 abilities, 349 skills and 591 observations as different layers. The September 2026 handout also describes 349 skills, 17 domains and 591 observations. The earlier Whitebook uses 344 skills across six domains. The dossier acknowledges architecture changes, but a complete crosswalk between versions was not supplied. Newer counts should not be attached retrospectively to validation of an older version.

standards.name: ICD-11 · health information
standards.text: A common classification and clinical terminology for recording, comparing and aggregating health information. It gives health-related records a consistent reference language.
standards.connection: Pinnacle’s dossier describes ICD-11 reference alignment; this does not make the software diagnostic.

standards.name: ICF · functioning and participation
standards.text: A framework covering body functions and structures, activities, participation and environmental context. It helps keep daily life and the support needed to participate in view.
standards.connection: Pinnacle’s handout and dossier describe ICF mappings. The dossier’s b-code examples describe body functions; activity, participation and environment need their own relevant codes.
standards.source: WHO · International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health

standards.name: ICHI · health interventions
standards.text: A classification for recording and analysing health interventions through their target, action and means. It can help describe what intervention is delivered in a consistent way.
standards.connection: Pinnacle’s dossier describes ICHI intervention coding within its architecture.
standards.source: WHO · International Classification of Health Interventions

standards.name: SNOMED CT · clinical terminology
standards.text: A detailed clinical terminology that represents information through concepts, descriptions and relationships. It supports consistent meaning in electronic clinical records.
standards.connection: Pinnacle’s dossier describes SNOMED CT terminology alignment. SNOMED International is the responsible organisation.
standards.source: SNOMED International · What is SNOMED CT?

sdgs.title: Health and well-being
sdgs.meaning: A mission to make developmental support clearer and more accessible to families.

sdgs.title: Quality education
sdgs.meaning: Early development, inclusive learning and support that helps children participate in education.

sdgs.title: Reduced inequalities
sdgs.meaning: Participation and inclusion, including for children with disabilities and their families.

sdgs.title: Partnerships for the goals
sdgs.meaning: A direction for accountable collaboration. Specific partnership achievements require named agreements and measured contributions.

architecture.title: 17 domains. 79 abilities. 349 skills.
architecture.intro: A broad view of development, organised into abilities and skills that can inform a child-specific plan. The direction is practical: what helps this child communicate, learn, manage daily routines and take part in life?

layers.name: Developmental domains
layers.meaning: The broad areas considered in Pinnacle’s framework.

layers.name: Abilities
layers.meaning: The capabilities the framework helps organise.

layers.name: Skills
layers.meaning: More detailed skills to connect with individual goals.

architecture.measurementMeaning: The company-described observation framework and score support a starting point and subsequent progress review. A child’s plan selects relevant priorities; the totals do not mean every child needs every intervention.
architecture.attribution: Pinnacle-defined architecture: company walkthrough, page 26; September handout, pages 5–6. The standards below supply classification and terminology; WHO does not define these numerical totals. An item-level domain–ability–skill crosswalk has not been independently audited in this review.

lifeGoals.title: Different starting points. Meaningful everyday goals.
lifeGoals.text: Families may arrive with questions about autism, ADHD, communication, sensory processing, movement, learning or other developmental concerns. Pinnacle’s stated purpose centres on the capabilities that help each child grow toward self-sufficiency and participate in mainstream life, with the support and accommodations they need.

goals.title: Communication and choice
goals.text: Express a need, make a choice and connect with other people.

goals.title: Daily-life independence
goals.text: Build participation in familiar routines and practise useful daily-living skills.

goals.title: Learning and belonging
goals.text: Take part in school, relationships and community with appropriate support.

lifeGoals.boundary: These are examples of individual goals, not promised results. Professional assessment identifies the support appropriate to each child; diagnosis and medical care remain important where indicated. The licensed software’s scope is non-diagnostic developmental support for ages 0–12, not treatment of every condition.

alignment.title: Pinnacle’s framework, connected to international languages
alignment.text: The Evidence Dossier describes mappings to ICD-11, ICF and ICHI, alongside SNOMED CT and LOINC terminology and HL7 FHIR representations. These are company-described architecture and mapping claims. Correctly implemented mappings can support more consistent records, exchange and analysis across settings.
alignment.boundary: The reviewed evidence does not include a complete item-by-item mapping audit or implementation-conformance report. Classification alignment does not establish WHO, UN or SNOMED endorsement, validate the developmental score, or expand the MD-5 intended use.
alignment.source: Evidence Dossier, pages 45–46, 84 and 86; September handout, pages 6 and 8

scaleReadiness.title: A population-scale ambition. One child’s life at the centre.
scaleReadiness.text: Pinnacle describes a connected developmental-support architecture designed for wider deployment: a common framework, a persistent child-specific record, guided daily practice and human review. Its potential value at scale is continuity—helping families and professionals work from the same developmental direction across home, therapy and school.
scaleReadiness.readinessText: For a health system, sovereign readiness means demonstrable control over data and operations under its own governance requirements. International readiness also needs validated mappings, appropriate local language and workflows, applicable regulatory permissions, and evidence of safe, useful performance in that setting.

requirements.title: Local control and accountability
requirements.text: Document hosting location, data-controller responsibilities, lawful use, consent, access controls and audit trails.

requirements.title: Interoperability in practice
requirements.text: Validate the mappings and test information exchange with the systems that will actually use it.

requirements.title: Capacity and real-world value
requirements.text: Test deployment performance, accessibility and child-centred outcomes in the intended population and setting.

scaleReadiness.evidence: The reviewed MD-5 and BIS scope establish specific regulatory and quality-system foundations. Reported network activity and information-security records add context. Together they support examining the deployment proposition; they are not a sovereign-grade certification or authorisation to operate in every country.
scaleReadiness.volumeBoundary: The reported 2.7 billion+ structured records count database rows and events. They do not establish a nationally representative population, verified AI-training volume or population-level clinical effectiveness.

parentRole.title: Parents are explicitly included in the licensed intended use.
parentRole.quote: The software is intended to assist parents, therapists, educators, and caregivers by providing developmental ability measurement, readiness tracking, progress forecasting, and adaptive therapy-plan support for children aged 0–12 years.
parentRole.meaning: Bring guided developmental practice into everyday life. The licensed intended use names parents and caregivers alongside therapists and educators. Families have an explicit role in using the software’s developmental-support functions, with goals and guidance appropriate to their child.
parentRole.connection: Pinnacle’s Everyday Therapy programme and Fusion Module describe how that participation connects with daily practice, feedback and professional review. The BIS schedule names parent, family and caregiver tracking and correction as part of the connected developmental journey.
parentRole.boundary: The intended use identifies whom the software assists and what it supports. It does not confer professional therapist credentials, register a home as a therapy centre or replace appropriate clinical care. A worldwide exclusivity claim is not established by these documents.

bisScopeQuote: Design, development, verification and validation, release, deployment, maintenance, technical support and post-market surveillance of Software as a Medical Device (SaMD), including Pinnacle AI GPT-OS™, and Developmental Support Software (Non-Diagnostic), including developmental ability mapping (Ability Score), prognostic engine Prognose®, Clinical Intervention Every Day Therapy Programme through Therapeutic AI®, Parent, Family, Caregiver, Therapist, Clinical Tracking and Correction Fusion Module, School Readiness, Speech Readiness, Motor Readiness, Study IQ Readiness, Behavior Readiness, Self Sufficiency Index, Mainstream Inclusion Index, 7 readiness indexing and associated digital developmental support modules for the full developmental lifecycle of children.

workflow.title: Your observations shape the next plan.
workflow.intro: PinnacleAI® connects measurement, a child-specific plan, guided everyday practice and feedback. The purpose is practical: help the child build abilities that matter at home, in school and in everyday life.

modules.name: AbilityScore®
modules.text: Bring observations into a structured view of the child’s present abilities and readiness.

modules.name: Personal Development Kernel + Prognose®
modules.text: Connect this child’s history, goals and responses to the next recommendations.

modules.name: TherapeuticAI® + Everyday Therapy™
modules.text: Turn goals into guided activities that the care team and family can put into practice.

modules.name: Fusion Module + reassessment
modules.text: Bring people’s feedback into review, adjust the plan and reassess progress over time.

workflow.continuity: One child’s history connects each cycle. What the family and professionals observe today informs what they review next.

details.question: Where do parents and the care team fit?
details.answer: Parents and caregivers contribute observations from everyday life; therapists and educators bring the context they see. The MD-5 intended use explicitly names parents, therapists, educators and caregivers. Their participation connects home routines with professional support.
details.note: The reviewed dossier describes the clinical AbilityScore® as clinician-administered and clinically governed. A family questionnaire should therefore be distinguished from the clinical assessment and score.

details.question: What is the Personal Development Kernel?
details.answer: It is the child-specific developmental record described in Pinnacle’s architecture: measurements, goals, responses to activities, environment and history stay connected. That record informs subsequent recommendations, so the next plan can take earlier experience into account.
details.note: For a family, the useful question is simple: how did what we observed last time change what we will do next?

details.question: How does a goal become everyday practice?
details.answer: The documented programme connects selected activities to the child’s goals and abilities. The September handout describes 7–9 daily techniques and a four-day therapy forecast. The methodology preprint describes programmes delivered four days ahead, giving families time to prepare.
details.note: The care team should explain the selected activities, demonstration and support appropriate to the child. Programme counts in different publications vary; the agreed individual plan determines what to practise.

details.question: What happens when an activity is too hard or does not engage the child?
details.answer: That experience is useful feedback. The methodology preprint describes 1–9-star technique ratings feeding the Personal Development Kernel. The BIS schedule names parent, family, caregiver, therapist and clinical tracking and correction through the Fusion Module. This makes review of the plan part of the described workflow. The dossier describes human oversight of recommendations; technique selection is not left to the system alone.
details.note: Illustrative example: the family records difficulty with an agreed communication activity; the care team reviews the observation, adjusts the activity or support, and reviews the response at the next check. This explains the feedback loop; it is not a patient case or a promised result.

sources.label: BIS schedule · tracking and correction scope

details.question: What should the monthly review make clearer?
details.answer: Compare the child’s present abilities with earlier assessments, discuss progress and difficulties, and agree the next priorities. The company walkthrough and methodology preprint describe monthly reassessment. A useful review connects the score with observable changes in the child’s daily life.
details.note: The BIS scope names seven readiness indexes: School Readiness, Speech Readiness, Motor Readiness, Study IQ Readiness, Behavior Readiness, Self Sufficiency Index and Mainstream Inclusion Index. These names describe the modules; they do not promise school entry or independence.

details.question: Who can access the child’s programme?
details.answer: The company describes parental-consent controls and role-based access for the clinical and caregiving people involved in the child’s programme. Access should support coordinated care while respecting the child and family’s privacy.
details.note: The dossier documents the access model. Families can ask their care team which people have access and how permissions and consent are managed for their child.

workflow.scope: This explains the workflow described in the cited documents. The MD-5 establishes the intended use of a non-diagnostic Class B device for ages 0–12; the BIS schedule names the software and quality-system scope. Research methods, workflow descriptions and evidence of clinical outcomes are different types of evidence.
workflow.versionNote: The supplied September report examples display AbilityScore® and all seven readiness indices on a 0–1000 scale; the overall cover identifies report presentation version V-1.6.9.9, separate from the SaMD software version. The older methodology preprint describes readiness indices on a 0–100 scale. These are version-specific descriptions and should not be combined without a crosswalk. The preprint also describes 400+ Personal Development Kernel data points, while the company walkthrough describes 4,000+ developmental data points; those counts need a current version-specific definition.

reportPack.title: One overall profile. Seven focused readiness reports.
reportPack.intro: The eight supplied report examples present an overall AbilityScore® and seven readiness indices on a 0–1000 display scale. Together, the overall profile and focused views give the family and care team a shared starting point for discussing priorities and the next plan.

reports.name: Speech Readiness Index
reports.meaning: A focused view to discuss communication priorities.

reports.name: Behavior Readiness Index
reports.meaning: A focused view to discuss behaviour and participation.

reports.name: Motor Readiness Index
reports.meaning: A focused view to discuss movement-related abilities.

reports.name: Study/IQ Readiness Index
reports.meaning: The report’s named view of readiness for learning.

reports.name: School Readiness Index
reports.meaning: A focused view to discuss preparation and support for school.

reports.name: Self-Sufficiency Index
reports.meaning: A focused view to discuss growing everyday independence.

reports.name: Mainstream Readiness Index
reports.meaning: A focused view to discuss participation with other people.

reportPack.review: Report titles checked against eight supplied examples on 19 September 2026. The overall report cover identifies report presentation version V-1.6.9.9. This is a review of report format, not an independent study of outcomes.
reportPack.privacy: This public guide describes the report structure. Children’s identities, individual results and original reports remain private.
reportPack.interpretation: Each index report includes an “Assessment By” field. Read the results with the assessment context and care-team explanation. Readiness-index titles are not diagnoses; the Study/IQ Readiness title should not be read as an independently established IQ test.
